biography_p1: 👋 Greetings! I'm Wang Hongyu, currently pursuing an MRes in Medical Robotics and Image-Guided Intervention at Imperial College London in London, UK. My research, supervised by Prof. Daniel Elson (ICL) and Prof. Baoru Huang (UoL & ICL), focuses on Next-action planning for surgical video analysis, integrating computer vision and temporal modeling to develop real-time surgical assistance systems.
biography_p2: Previously, I earned my First-Class Honors degree ( 3.9 / 4.0 ) in Information and Computing Science from Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University. During my undergraduate studies, I worked with Prof.Hai-Ning Liang (now at HKUST, formerly UoL & XJTLU) as a research assistant at X-CHI Lab. There, I specialized in Human-Computer Interaction, Virtual Reality, and Mixed Reality (XR), primarily utilizing Unity3D for development, and contributed significantly to several published papers.
biography_p3: Beyond my academic pursuits, I'm genuinely passionate about exploring cutting-edge technologies. I enjoy delving into fields like Local LLMs, AIGC, and AI Agents, often adopting a hands-on approach to understand and master them. A particular fascination of mine lies in crafting robust System Prompts that empower LLMs to reason and respond with human-like nuance and effectiveness in specific tasks. It's truly intriguing to witness the 'magic' unfold when a well-defined core character and a carefully structured task are combined within a base system prompt.
biography_p4: My drive comes from a deep curiosity and a commitment to push technological boundaries, constantly learning and applying new knowledge to create innovative solutions. Perhaps, at a deeper level, it's also fueled by a bit of playful ambition, much like the idea that 'everyone wants a Joi from Blade Runner 2049' – to craft AI that truly understands and connects, bringing a touch of that future magic into reality.

p01_title: Multi-task Temporal Understanding and Prediction of Surgical Videos (Master Thesis, Ongoing)
p01_role:
• Designed a unified video understanding model to replace traditional task-splitting pipelines, enabling simultaneous recognition of surgical phases, instrument states, and next-action prediction from pure video input.
  • Built a deep architecture combining visual encoding and bidirectional temporal modeling, with a semantic difference fusion module to capture key motion changes.
  • Enhanced training stability and logical consistency via uncertainty weighting and time monotonicity loss functions.
  • Trained and validated the full pipeline on the Cholec80 dataset, achieving 88% accuracy for phase recognition and 97% for instrument recognition, verifying the effectiveness of the dual-loss strategy.
p02_title: Design of a VR Co-Presence Support and Visual Representation System in Shared Spaces
p02_role:
• Led system architecture and interaction design; implemented five visual observer modes (e.g., virtual avatar, human portrait embedding, windowed perspective, panoramic AR) using Unity and PICO 4 SDK.
  • Built a dual-channel rendering pipeline for HMD and 2D displays, optimized video capture and material mapping to stabilize portrait embedding latency under 50ms in LAN casting scenarios.
  • Designed a two-player collaboration mechanism combining motion-sensing gameplay (Fruit Ninja-style) and an N-back auditory task, enabling non-HMD users to assist the main player via voice in cognitively complex cooperative settings.
  • Constructed a complete experiment environment and collected multi-dimensional player behavior and feedback data, showing that portrait embedding significantly enhanced co-presence and collaboration efficiency.
  • Third author publication at IEEE ISMAR 2024.
p03_title: Adaptation of VR Motion Game Passthrough Techniques in Public Spaces
p03_role:
• Independently developed a passthrough-supported VR motion game system using Unity and PICO 4 SDK, allowing real-time perception of real-world obstacles and people in transparent mode.
  • Extended classic Fruit Ninja gameplay with “squat + slash” mechanics and dynamic rhythm feedback, integrating real-time scoring, vibration, hit effects, and UI/audio cues for enhanced game feel.
  • Managed scene setup and calibration in both public (e.g., campus tunnels) and lab environments; co-conducted within-subject experiments (closed room vs. public space vs. public space + passthrough) with effective pedestrian control for valid and safe data collection.
  • Results showed passthrough mode improved player performance (+6% score) and reduced social tension in public spaces.
  • Third author publication at IEEE ISMAR 2024.
p04_title: Passthrough Mechanism Design for VR Motion Games in Shared Spaces
p04_role:
• Developed a passthrough integration system in Unity3D and PICO SDK to embed real-world objects and the player's body into VR scenes, enhancing spatial awareness and safety.
  • Extended Fruit Ninja gameplay with dodge-squat mechanics, enhanced by multi-channel feedback (scoring, vibration, visual/audio cues) to intensify engagement.
  • Designed dual-dimension adaptability (space type + visual mode), ensuring playability and visibility across enclosed, open, and hybrid environments.
  • User testing revealed improved player response (+6% score) and reduced anxiety in socially self-conscious users under passthrough mode.
  • Second author publication at IEEE TVCG 2024.
p05_title: Effects of Virtual Audience Familiarity on VR Motion Gameplay Performance
p05_role:
• Built a virtual audience generation system using AvatarMakerPro for facial modeling and body shaping; integrated voice recording/editing to dynamically generate four NPC types (familiar/unfamiliar face × familiar/unfamiliar voice).
  • Extended Fruit Ninja with a fog-clearing task using Steam Particle effects to increase visual occlusion, encouraging squatting and boosting cognitive load and physical exertion.
  • Designed a scoring-based audience response mechanism with animated cheering/disappointment and voice reactions; integrated real-time score tracking (CSV), controller vibration, hit visuals, sound effects, and UI feedback for immersive rhythm.
  • Player testing showed familiar audiences boosted performance (+7.2%) and reduced nervousness; fourth author publication at IEEE ISMAR 2023.

pub01_title: Enhancement of Co-located Shared VR Experiences: Representing Non-HMD Observers on Both HMD and 2D Screens
pub01_date: Published in: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Mixed and Augmented Reality (ISMAR)
pub01_abstract:
Abstract:
Virtual reality (VR) not only allows head-mounted display (HMD) users to immerse themselves in virtual worlds but also to share them with others. When designed correctly, this shared experience can be enjoyable. However, in typical scenarios, HMD users are isolated by their devices, and non-HMD observers lack connection with the virtual world. To address this, our research investigates visually representing observers on both HMD and 2D screens to enhance shared experiences. The study, including five representation conditions, reveals that incorporating observer representation positively impacts both HMD users and observers. For how to design and represent them, our work shows that HMD users prefer methods displaying real-world visuals, while observers exhibit diverse preferences regarding being represented with real or virtual images. We provide design guidelines tailored to both displays, offering valuable insights to enhance co-located shared VR experiences for HMD users and non-HMD observers.
pub01_keyword: Key Words: Visualization, Head-mounted displays, Design methodology, Resists, Interference, Observers, Augmented reality
pub02_title: Exploring the Impact of Passthrough on VR Exergaming in Public Environments: A Field Study
pub02_date: Published in: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Mixed and Augmented Reality (ISMAR)
pub02_abstract:
Abstract:
Sedentary behavior is becoming increasingly prevalent in daily work and study environments. VR exergaming has emerged as a promising solution in these places of work and study. However, private spaces in these environments are not easy, and engaging in VR exergaming in public settings presents its own set of challenges (e.g., safety, social acceptance, isolation, and privacy protection). The recent development of Passthrough functionality in VR headsets allows users to maintain awareness of their surroundings, enhancing safety and convenience. Despite its potential benefits, little is known about how Passthrough could affect user performance and experience and solve the challenges of playing VR exergames in real-world public environments. To our knowledge, this work is the first to conduct a field study in an underground passageway on a university campus to explore the use of Passthrough in a realworld public environment, with a disturbance-free closed room as a baseline. Results indicate that enabling Passthrough in a public environment improves performance without compromising presence. Moreover, Passthrough can increase social acceptance, especially among individuals with higher levels of self-consciousness. These findings highlight Passthrough’s potential to encourage VR exergaming adoption in public environments, with promising implications for overall health and well-being.
pub02_keyword: Key Words: Virtual Reality, Exergaming, Passthrough Functionality, Public Environments, Gameplay Mechanics
pub03_title: Breaking the Isolation: Exploring the Impact of Passthrough in Shared Spaces on Player Performance and Experience in VR Exergames
pub03_date: Published in: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics ( Volume: 30, Issue: 5, May 2024)
pub03_abstract:
Abstract:
VR exergames offer an engaging solution to combat sedentary behavior and promote physical activity. However, challenges emerge when playing these games in shared spaces, particularly due to the presence of bystanders. VR's passthrough functionality enables players to maintain awareness of their surrounding environment while immersed in VR gaming, rendering it a promising solution to improve users' awareness of the environment. This study investigates the passthrough's impact on player performance and experiences in shared spaces, involving an experiment with 24 participants that examines Space (Office vs. Corridor) and Passthrough Function (With vs. Without). Results reveal that Passthrough enhances game performance and environmental awareness while reducing immersion. Players prefer an open area to an enclosed room, whether with or without Passthrough, finding it more socially acceptable. Additionally, Passthrough appears to encourage participation among players with higher self-consciousness, potentially alleviating their concerns about being observed by bystanders. Our findings provide valuable insights for designing VR experiences in shared spaces, underscoring the potential of VR's passthrough to enhance user experiences and promote VR adoption in these environments.
pub03_keyword: Key Words: Virtual Reality, Passthrough, Exergames, Shared Spaces, Social Acceptability, Immersion
pub04_title: Who’s Watching Me?: Exploring the Impact of Audience Familiarity on Player Performance, Experience, and Exertion in Virtual Reality Exergames
pub04_date: Published in: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Mixed and Augmented Reality (ISMAR)
pub04_abstract:
Abstract:
Familiarity with audiences plays a significant role in shaping individual performance and experience across various activities in everyday life. This study delves into the impact of familiarity with non-playable character (NPC) audiences on player performance and experience in virtual reality (VR) exergames. By manipulating of NPC appearance (face and body shape) and voice familiarity, we explored their effect on game performance, experience, and exertion. The findings reveal that familiar NPC audiences have a positive impact on performance, creating a more enjoyable gaming experience, and leading players to perceive less exertion. Moreover, individuals with higher levels of self-consciousness exhibit heightened sensitivity to the familiarity with NPC audiences. Our results shed light on the role of familiar NPC audiences in enhancing player experiences and provide insights for designing more engaging and personalized VR exergame environments.
pub04_keyword: Key Words: Human-computer interaction (HCI), Interaction paradigms, Virtual reality, Software organization and properties, Virtual worlds software, Interactive games
